**Summary of the Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) Class Aircraft Carrier Program Report**

This report outlines the background, current status, and potential oversight issues for Congress regarding the Navy’s Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) class aircraft carrier program. The Navy’s proposed FY2019/FY2020 budgets request billions in procurement funding for the program, with congressional decisions significantly impacting Navy capabilities, future funding requirements, and the domestic shipbuilding industrial base.

**Force Structure and the CVN-75 RCOH**
Federal law mandates a minimum of 11 operational aircraft carriers and 9 carrier air wings. In December 2016, the Navy established a new force-level goal of 355 ships, including 12 carriers. However, the Navy’s FY2020 budget submission proposed early retirement of the *Harry S. Truman* (CVN-75) around FY2024 by defunding its mid-life Refueling Complex Overhaul (RCOH). This would have temporarily dropped the fleet to 10 carriers and 8 air wings. On April 30, 2019, the Administration withdrew this proposal, opting to fund the RCOH and keep the ship in service past FY2024. 

**Procurement and the Two-Ship Block Buy**
The Navy plans to procure at least four Ford-class carriers. 
*   **CVN-78 (*Gerald R. Ford*):** Commissioned in 2017, the ship's estimated procurement cost is $13.1 billion. 
*   **CVN-79 (*John F. Kennedy*):** Procured in FY2013, construction is 55% complete, with delivery scheduled for 2024. 
*   **CVN-80 (*Enterprise*) & CVN-81:** Authorized for a two-ship block buy contract in January 2019, the Navy estimates this strategy will save nearly $3 billion to $4 billion compared to purchasing the ships individually.

This classification affects year-to-year ship procurement comparisons, the 30-year shipbuilding plan profile, and the executability of funds under a continuing resolution (CR).

The provision permitted the Navy to add CVN-81 to the existing contract for building CVN-80 after the Department of Defense (DOD) made certain certifications to Congress. DOD made the certifications on December 31, 2018, and the Navy announced the award of the contract on January 31, 2019. CVN-80 was procured in FY2018. The Navy's proposed FY2020 budget estimates the ship's procurement cost at $12,335.1 million (i.e., about $12.3 billion) in then-year dollars. The ship received AP funding in FY2016 and FY2017, and the Navy plans to fully fund the ship in FY2018-FY2025 using incremental funding authorized by Section 121(c) of P.L. 115-232.
